Q: How can I integrate Google Analytics 4 data with digital marketing KPIs for actionable campaign insights? A:

1. Define Clear Marketing KPIs First

Before using GA4 data, identify what success looks like for your campaigns. Common KPIs include:

Website traffic & user growth

Conversion rate

Cost per lead (CPL)

Engagement rate

Bounce rate

Revenue & ROI

User retention

Each KPI should match your campaign goal (leads, sales, awareness, etc.).

2. Set Up GA4 Events & Conversions

GA4 works on an event-based model, so proper tracking is crucial.

Track events such as:

Page views

Button clicks

Form submissions

Purchases

Scroll depth

Video engagement

Mark important actions as Conversions (e.g., lead form submitted, purchase completed).

This helps directly connect campaign performance with business outcomes.

3. Connect GA4 with Marketing Platforms

Integrate GA4 with:

Google Ads → Track ad performance & conversions

Google Search Console → Measure organic traffic & keyword impact

Meta Ads / LinkedIn Ads (via UTM tracking)

CRM tools (optional for advanced tracking)

Use UTM parameters to track:

Campaign source

Medium

Campaign name

Content & keywords

This helps identify which channel drives the best results.

Q: Accessing Github packages with Fine-grained personal access tokens A:

There is no workaround here :

GitHub Packages only supports authentication using personal access tokens, this is explicitly stated in GitHub’s own documentation, and fine-grained PATs simply are not supported for packages read /write today;

the only supported way to avoid a classic PAT is using GITHUB_TOKEN inside GitHub Actions, which works only in Actions and nowhere else, so for local dev or external CI a classic PAT with minimal packages scopes is still mandatory, even if your org has moved to fine-grained tokens.

Q: How to create a JSON-only API route using React Router framework on Vercel? A:

React Router does support JSON-only “resource routes”, but they do not work on Vercel if your app is deployed as a static Vite build. In that case, you need a Vercel Serverless Function.

When you deploy a React Router v7 + Vite app on Vercel, it’s served as a static site by default. That means:

  • loader / action functions never run on the server

  • /api/bookings falls back to index.html

  • you get Unexpected token '<' or a 404

So the problem isn’t your route code, it’s the deployment mode.

React Router v7 supports resource routes (routes with only loader / action and no UI), but they only work when React Router is running on a server (SSR / server adapter).

They are not executed in a static Vite deployment on Vercel.

Use a Vercel Serverless Function for /api/*

// api/bookings.ts
import type { VercelRequest, VercelResponse } from "@vercel/node";

export default function handler(req: VercelRequest, res: VercelResponse) {
  if (req.method === "GET") {
    return res.json({ bookings: [] });
  }

  res.status(405).end();
}

Client usage stays the same:

fetch("/api/bookings").then(r => r.json());

Hope this help
